title: Tor bounds detected on pro-etale covers and open-closed decompositions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For integers $c\leq d$, say that a complex has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ when its derived tensor with every module sheaf in degree zero has zero cohomology outside $[c,d]$; use K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$ use the inverse-image ring $f^{-1}A$ and module inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. (i) If $\{V_i\to X\}$ is a pro-étale covering family and every $K|_{V_i}$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. (ii) If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion], and $i^{-1}K,j^{-1}K$ have Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. No quasi-coherence, Noetherian or finite-cover hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Locality and Strata, detecting vanishing after restriction rather than invoking an additional projection formula
